findings.proposed_english_tex:
\begin{proof}
The fixed-arity construction in the paragraph
\emph{Dense primitive hosts and their exact weights} of
Section~\ref{p14:comp:confinement} proves the dense host count,
uniformly over all true windows and deterministic subfamilies.
Its parameters are fixed before $N$.
For a primitive family, projection injectivity gives
$\rho(I)\le\min_{x\in I}d_x\le L$. Since $p_x\le2p\ll_C N^{-1}$
and $2^L\ll_C N$, each exact weight is $O_{r,C}(N^{1-r})$.
The dense host count therefore gives the stated dense mass.

For the full sum, fix a small $\xi>0$ and split at $\rho=\xi L$.
Below the threshold, Corollary~\ref{p13:half:connected} bounds
the independent mass by $O(N^{-r/2+\varepsilon'})$;
the additional rank factor is $O_C(N^\xi)$.
Above it, the dense bound with parameter $\xi$ gives
$O(N^{1-r+\varepsilon'})$. As $r\ge3$, $1-r<-r/2$.
Choose $\xi,\varepsilon'$ within the requested final margin.
Finally, for a primitive family,
$c(I)=q(I)-\prod_{x\in I}p_x$ and $q(I)$ is either zero or
$2^{\rho(I)}\prod_{x\in I}p_x$. Hence the actual joint and
absolute centered sums have the same powers.
All arities in this argument are fixed; the separate
all-cardinality certificate estimates are still required.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
The assumed threshold implies $x\ge2B$.

findings.proposed_english_tex:
\paragraph{Two further optimal powers.}
For every fixed channel height $h\ge3$,
Theorem~\ref{p13:channels:hierarchy} gives the error of the
explicit quadratic reference retaining all channels through height $h$:
the first omitted height $h+1$ contributes order
$LN^{-h/(h+1)}$, with an explicit moving coefficient.
These finite-reference powers differ from the optimal power $4/3$
for exact cumulants; $h$ is fixed before $N$.

Theorem~\ref{p13:third:main} identifies the optimal power $41/30$
of the third factorial cumulant. Its positive lower bound comes
from genuine compatible triples of type $10:12:15$,
and its upper bound includes all triples.
No full asymptotic constant for that cumulant is claimed.

findings.proposed_english_tex:
\begin{proof}
The algebraic form of Lemma~\ref{p13:transfer:conversion}
also allows arbitrary real pair coefficients.
Apply it with common marginal $p$ and a coefficient $C_2$
on one fixed pair, all other pair coefficients being zero.
The reference is $b^{*n}+C_2\Delta^{*2}*b^{*(n-2)}$,
and its absolute pair mass is $|C_2|$.
It differs from $Q_{\mu,\alpha_G}$ by
$O_C(np^3+(np^2)^2+|C_2|(np^2+p))$.
Replacing $C_2$ by $\beta_N$ costs at most
$4|\beta_N-C_2|$, since $b^{*(n-2)}$ has norm one.
Now $n=O(N)$, $p=O_C(N^{-1})$ and $C_2=O_C(a_N)$.
These bounds give the stated error.
\end{proof}
findings.additional_english_tex:
The same algebraic bound holds for arbitrary real coefficients $c(e)$
on pairs, with $A_2=\sum_e|c(e)|$ and
$\alpha=2\sum_e c(e)-s_2$.
Their interpretation as covariances is needed only to identify
$\alpha$ with the second factorial cumulant.

\section*{Formalization and statement correspondence}
The repository \url{https://github.com/Vulkin-prog/paper-p1-lean}
contains the Lean development for both texts, checked with
Lean~4.36.0-rc2 and the pinned Mathlib revision.
It records the exact statements, their proof entries, and the
validation sources; the version~1.6 archive is preserved.

Version~1.7 corrected two false original formulations:
the enclosing-interval radius in Lemma~\ref{p1:arith:asymmetric}
and the capped exponent in Lemma~\ref{p13:short:quadratic}.
Their counterexamples and corrected scopes are discussed beside
those results in the companion. Version~1.8 selectively integrates
stronger estimates and shorter proofs; it retains all 167
numbered-result labels and their numbering.
Intermediate proof constructions in the change ledger are not
all separate scientific contributions.

Kernel checking and finite diagnostics do not replace checking
the correspondence between the formal and printed statements.
The audited proofs use only the standard kernel axioms recorded
in the repository. This working draft has no Palomar identifier.

common_homogeneous_envelope_followup.proposed_english_tex:
Write $q_0(I)$ for the probability of the homogeneous events,
with zero right-hand side in place of the affine start prescription.
Exact factorization gives
\[
 q_0(I)=2^{\rho_{\rm rel}(I)}\prod_{x\in I}2^{-d_x}
       \le 2^r p^r2^{\rho_{\rm rel}(I)},\qquad |I|=r,
\]
because local rigidity gives $d_x\ge L-1$.
The nominal fixed-size estimates therefore imply the same powers
for the true homogeneous mass: $N^{-r/2+\varepsilon}$ in general
and $N^{1-r+\varepsilon}$ when $\rho_{\rm rel}\ge\eta L$.
Here $r$ and $\eta>0$ are fixed before $N$; the factor $2^r$
is absorbed using a smaller fixed error margin.
The original exact rank weights, actual joint probabilities,
and absolute centered coefficients are each bounded by $q_0(I)$.
Thus one homogeneous envelope controls all four sums, even when
an original affine system is incompatible or has a zero marginal.
